chapter: Hampton, New York and Lee's own band
title: Sunday jam sessions at Billy Berg's and the $500 union fine
summary: Lee ran jam sessions, was fined $500 after one that brought in players from the Ellington and Lunceford bands, and lived next to the Union.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: You know? There was a band on recording, so anyway -- they heard about us back east. But to tell you more about Billy Berg's, I used to give jam sessions there every Sunday. Now, I would call the musicians. What would happen, well -- I was fined once $500 because in Los Angeles, they did not want you to jam, you know, and as I stated earlier, I always carried my drums around with me, and wherever someone was playing, I would play, you know, and I

lived next door to the Union, you know, and -- I lived at 1706 Central -- and 1710 was the Musicians Union. And I was before the Board every time the Board would meet, because I wouldn't stop jamming. And they said they were gonna fine me, you know, but I mean, I was like an adopted child of theirs that was bad and was gonna keep doing it.

And so the biggest session I had -- they did fine me this time. It was out here, you know -- out here in California the bars close at 2 o'clock, so what I did, is I invited -- there was, a guy had a trio called -- Lorenzo Flournoy Flinney had a trio, and Nellie Letcher had her trio, and Luncford Luntswood was here at the time, and Duke was here at the time.

So they brought 5 or 6 musicians; you know, Ben Webster and then came with Blanton, and Sonny Greer and Rex Stewart Stuart; they came in during the night, and I invited everybody from the clubs, but only performers and musicians could come. And the place was loaded; they came from the Belle Tavern, in Gardenia, there was a Belle Tavern in Gardenia, which I didn't tell you earlier ... there was a musician, he was a guitarist; his name was C.B. Burke; I think he wrote "When the Swallows Come Back to Capistrano" -- his name was Ceele Burke, and he had the band out at the Belle Tavern, and they had the people, the clubs all over town, all the chorus girls, all the principals, they came in, because I invited everybody. Everybody.

But the big thing was that Lunceford Luntz was in town, and Duke was in town, because Duke was in town because he was doing downtown the show which ran quite a while. They got 5 or 6 men from each one of their bands, and then the trios would play, and then we would close it, you know. And naturally, it was kind of a mismatch, because we would burn them up -- because we had all these arrangements, you know, and they were from a big band and we were from a small band.
